papers.title: The rise and diversification of spidroins in the deep-time evolution of spiders.
papers.abstract: The evolutionary success of spiders is often attributed to their stunning ability to produce and utilize silk, but the potential link between the molecular and phenotypic basis of silk production and spider diversification is seldom tested in a robust dated phylogenetic framework. Here, we provide a macroevolutionary context for testing hypotheses by reconstructing and dating the spider tree of life using genomic and transcriptomic data. We searched exhaustively for members of the spider silk protein (spidroin) gene family from omics data and identified them in an iterative phylogenetic pipeline. Four distinct new types of spidroins with atypical sequence characteristics are discovered to be widespread in true spiders with the potential to affect silk properties, as inferred by our phylogenetic generalized linear mixed model and phylogenetic generalized least squares analyses. Combining our robust dated phylogenomic tree of spiders and a comprehensive spidroin dataset, a comprehensive picture of spidroin evolution is revealed. By performing state speciation and extinction analyses, we discovered that only the presence of aggregate gland is linked to a higher diversification rate among all binary spidroin-related characters, while the speciation rate of spiders is dependent on the number of ampullate-gland-associated-atypical spidroin types, silk gland types, total spidroin copies, and total spidroin types.

papers.title: Enacted love: Capitalization responses signal love, including toward strangers.
papers.abstract: What behavior is seen as "love" and why does it matter? We theorize active-constructive responding to another's disclosure of good news is prototypical "enacted love" and test hypotheses about implications for a loving person's relationship development. We use three distinct methods-dyadic interactions between romantic couples (Study 1, N = 160), real spontaneous responses to a stranger's good news (Study 2, N = 204), and observation of others' real capitalization responses to a stranger's good news (Studies 3-5, N = 97, 105, and 402, respectively)-to assess convergent and discriminant evidence for the construct. Study 2 uses experience sampling to track the development of capitalization respondents' social lives over time. Studies 4 and 5 use within-subjects experiments to test hypotheses that loving behavior could influence others' interactions with loving people. Results have theoretical implications for close relationships and the concept of "loving one's neighbor," plus practical implications for building bridges in a divided society. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Longitudinal associations between romantic relationship involvement and quality, depression, and suicidal ideation among bisexual women.
papers.journal: Journal of family psychology : JFP : journal of the Division of Family Psychology of the American Psychological Association (Division 43)
papers.abstract: Bisexual women have an increased likelihood of experiencing suicidal ideation (SI) and depressive symptoms than both heterosexual and lesbian women. Evidence suggests romantic relationship involvement may lead to worse mental health outcomes for bisexual individuals, even though it is frequently cited as a protective factor among heterosexual and lesbian/gay individuals. It is currently unknown whether romantic relationship involvement is associated with SI among bisexual women and whether other aspects of the romantic relationship (e.g., quality, partner gender) influence mental health in this population. The present study used up to eight waves of data from bisexual young women (N = 390 across waves) who participated in a longitudinal cohort study and identified as bisexual during at least two consecutive waves (range = 2-8 waves; M = 3.96, SD = 1.93). Multilevel modeling was used to assess concurrent and lagged associations between relationship involvement, quality, partner gender, and mental health. Relationship involvement was not significantly associated with depression or SI in concurrent or lagged analyses. In contrast, at the between-person level, participants who reported higher relationship support (on average) reported lower depressive symptoms, and participants who reported having a female partner more often (on average) reported lower depressive symptoms and SI in concurrent analyses. The present findings suggest that relationship quality and partner gender, but not relationship involvement, are associated with depressive symptoms and SI among bisexual women. As such, relationship quality may be a useful intervention target to improve the mental health of bisexual women. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: The cognitive developmental cascade at different timescales: Relationships among intrasubject variability, processing speed, working memory, and fluid intelligence in children aged 8 to 14 years.
papers.abstract: According to the developmental cascade model (Fry & Hale, 2000), accelerations in processing speed (PS) throughout childhood lead to improvements in working memory (WM) which in turn result in increased fluid intelligence (gf). Decreasing intrasubject variability (ISV) of reaction times has been proposed to play a crucial role within this cascade. While most of the evidence supporting the developmental cascade is derived from cross-sectional studies, longitudinal studies are scarce, with heterogeneous findings. Moreover, longitudinal analysis of correlational patterns may produce biased results, if within-person changes (development within the studied timeframe) are not separated from between-person variance (stable differences and long-term changes beyond the studied time frame). To overcome these limitations, N = 173 children aged 8-12 years at baseline (M ± SD: 10.01 ± 1.11, 51% female) were tested five times within 2.5 years using a computer-based testing battery including choice reaction time tasks to measure PS and ISV as well as span, operation span, and coordination tasks to measure WM. Cattell's Culture Fair Test was administered to measure gf. Separating between-person variance from within-person developmental changes using a cross-lagged panel model with random intercepts, the postulated close relationships between PS, ISV, WM, and gf were observed at the level of between-person differences on a long-term timescale alongside no evidence of the expected associations of within-person changes for a time frame of 2.5 years. Thus, associations consistent with the developmental cascade model may reflect stable between-person differences rather than short-term within-person changes. This has important implications for developmental theory and methodology. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Direct atomic-scale observation reveals rare earth element fractionation at mineral-water interfaces.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Clay minerals, ubiquitous across diverse geological systems, exert fundamental controls on critical geochemical processes, particularly through their adsorptive interactions with economically vital elements such as heavy rare earth elements (HREEs). The adsorption of HREEs onto clay surfaces is not only the key process that enriches these critical resources but also a potential archive for dating significant weathering events. However, the atomic-scale mechanisms governing the preferential adsorption and fractionation of rare earth elements (REEs) at mineral-water interfaces have remained poorly constrained. Here, employing in situ atomic-scale imaging via high-resolution atomic force microscopy, we systematically investigate the adsorption behaviors of light and heavy REEs (La, Y, Yb) onto key crystallographic planes-Si-basal, Al-basal, and edge terminations-of representative clay minerals (kaolinite, illite, mica) under environmentally relevant conditions (pH 4.8 to 6.4). We directly visualize and quantitatively reveal that Si-basal planes selectively enrich HREEs with pH-enhanced adsorption capacity, whereas Al-basal planes exhibit negligible REE adsorption below pH 5.8 but preferential HREE adsorption at pH 6.4. Integrating synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we identify the adsorption mechanism of REE on Si-basal and Al-basal/edge planes as outer-sphere complexation and inner-sphere binding, respectively. Furthermore, we quantify the contributions of distinct planes via surface complexation modeling, revealing Si-dominated to Al- and edge-controlled adsorption with elevating pH. These atomic-scale findings not only resolve long-standing debates about clay mineral-mediated REE fractionation but also redefine fundamental paradigms of surface reactivity at silicate mineral-water interfaces, offering insights into the cycling and metallogeny of other critical metals in aqueous and sedimentary environments.

papers.title: "Up-armoring" Military Couples: a Randomized Trial of a Preventive, Online Couple Intervention.
papers.journal: Prevention science : the official journal of the Society for Prevention Research
papers.abstract: This study tested whether access to a self-directed, online couple intervention offered preventively lessened the occurrence of future negative relationship outcomes (i.e., relationship dysfunction, infidelity, intimate partner violence [IPV]) for partnered service members in comparison to the usual resources for relationship assistance in the military. Participants were active duty military in a committed romantic relationship of at least 6-month duration (N = 581; 37.2% married) who had recently completed basic military training and were transitioning into technical training to learn a specific job skill set. Participants were randomly assigned by in-processing week to the intervention or the control condition. The intervention effect was modeled using both intent to treat (ITT) and complier average causal effect (CACE) approaches. None of the hypothesized intervention effects was significant in the ITT models. In contrast, the CACE analyses showed that compliers in the intervention group, defined as participants who created a specific action plan to improve a relationship target, compared with those in the control group who the analyses infer would have created an action plan, scored significantly lower on relationship distress and odds of perpetrating IPV at 6- and 12-month follow-ups. The trial was retrospectively registered with ClinicalTrials.gov on 18 April 2025 (ID: NCT06948877).

papers.title: Youth Engagements with Pornographic Stereotypes: A Systematic Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Pornography is a pervasive influence on young people's understandings and experiences of sexuality, raising critical questions about how they engage with its stereotypical portrayals. While most research approaches this issue from an "effects" perspective, far less is known about the more agentic, interpretive, and contextual ways in which youth make sense of and position themselves in relation to pornographic stereotypes. To address this gap, this systematic scoping review synthesizes empirical insights into how youth (aged 16-25) in OECD countries interpret and navigate such stereotypes. Following the PRISMA-ScR framework, a systematic search across eight academic databases identified 27 studies relevant to our research question. The findings show that youth engagement with pornographic stereotypes is heterogeneous, ranging from uncritical adoption of stereotypical scripts to various forms of detachment and transformation. These modes of engagement reveal both a capacity for evaluative reflection and the relational character of sexual socialization, with transformation, in particular, emerging through dialogue and boundary setting within peer and intimate relationships. By integrating dispersed findings, this review advances scholarly debates on media and sexuality while offering practical insights for interventions such as porn literacy programs.

papers.title: Expanded comparative genomics supports labial gland disease viruses as a distinct and deeply divergent lineage within Naldaviricetes.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Labial gland disease viruses (LGDVs) are recently identified dsDNA viruses infecting ants, but their diversity, genomic coherence, and taxonomic boundaries have remained unresolved. Here, we expanded LGDV members by mining public arthropod genome assemblies and sequencing field-collected ants. Novel LGDV genomes were recovered from Pheidole selathorax, Proformica mongolica, Messor orientalis, and geographically distinct Anoplolepis gracilipes populations. Comparative genomic analyses demonstrate that LGDVs retain the conserved core genes in the order Lefavirales, class Naldaviricetes, share additional conservative genes with Apis mellifera filamentous virus and related viruses (AmFV/AmFLV), and encode an LGDV-restricted conservative gene set. Amino acid identity, conservative site, and gene neighborhood analyses support the internal coherence of LGDVs while distinguishing them from AmFV/AmFLV, which retained only partial local gene neighborhood similarities and lacked detectable genome-wide macrosynteny with LGDVs. Phylogenies inferred by protein sequences and structures were broadly congruent, showing that predicted protein structures retained complementary lineage-discriminating signal across deeply divergent naldaviricetes, and recovering LGDVs as a monophyletic sister group to AmFV/AmFLV. Molecular dating further supported a deep separation between these lineages, indicating that LGDVs and AmFV/AmFLV represent distinct, long-term divergent groups rather than recent derivatives of one another. Collectively, these findings support LGDVs as an internally coherent, deeply divergent, and ant-associated virus family in the order Lefavirales, class Naldaviricetes. IMPORTANCE: Large dsDNA viruses within the class Naldaviricetes encompass deeply divergent lineages. The recent discovery of LGDVs suggests that these ant-associated viruses have a closer evolutionary relationship to the phylogenetically isolated honey bee-associated AmFV/AmFLV than other Naldavir

papers.title: Walrus population-specific marine reservoir offsets (ΔR) for calibration of radiocarbon dates: Implications for Arctic chronologies and medieval trade.
papers.abstract: Walruses have long played a vital role in Arctic subsistence and commercial economies, yet accurate radiocarbon dating of walrus-derived archaeological materials is complicated by regional variation in marine reservoir effects. This study presents new ΔR values derived from 31 new and 15 legacy radiocarbon dates on known-age walrus specimens spanning multiple populations of Odobenus rosmarus rosmarus and O. r. divergens. The results reveal substantial inter-population variability, with ΔR values ranging from -140 (Franz Josef Land) to +295 (Pacific), underscoring the importance of population-specific calibration. A pooled ΔR of +17±12 was calculated for western Greenland and the Canadian Arctic-regions central to the medieval Norse ivory trade-and applied to 12 walrus rostra and ivory artefacts excavated in Trondheim, Norway. The resulting calibrated dates are from the 11th to early 14th centuries CE, confirming that seemingly anomalous post-15th-century finds are residual rather than evidence of continued trade. An alternative ΔR estimate of -110 ± 35, derived solely from archaeological context dates, suggests potential time lags between harvest and deposition. These findings demonstrate the value of known-age walrus ΔR data for refining chronologies of Arctic exploitation and long-distance trade, while highlighting the need for provenance studies in archaeological dating and both the pertinence and limitations of mollusc-based reservoir corrections.

papers.title: Starch-concentration-controlled growth of anisotropic bismuth nanoplates: a facile and bio-assisted aqueous route to morphology-tuned optical response.
papers.abstract: Herein, we report a bio-assisted aqueous synthesis of single-crystalline, anisotropic bismuth (Bi0) nanoplates using starch as a dual reductant/kinetic regulator and poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (PVP) as a facet-selective capping agent. Powder XRD confirms the formation of rhombohedral elemental bismuth (JCPDS Card No. 44-1246) with no detectable crystalline impurity phases. Systematic evaluation of synthesis parameters reveals a surface-energy-driven growth mechanism governed by a kinetic and capping interplay. Lower starch concentrations produce predominantly quasi-spherical nanoparticles (∼80 nm) alongside minor polyhedral structures, whereas higher starch feeds favor the formation of uniform hexagonal nanoplates with lateral diagonal dimensions of 145-240 nm. Concurrently, lower PVP feeds result in mixed morphologies containing irregular nanoplates (∼115 nm), whereas increasing the PVP feed promotes effective facet passivation, increasing the prevalence of uniform hexagonal nanoplates (120-145 nm). Time-dependent observations show an initial stage at 2 h consisting of a mixed morphology (∼145 nm) that progresses beyond 2 h into predominantly uniform hexagonal nanoplates (∼200 nm), exhibiting a visibly increased thickness plates at 24 h consistent with Ostwald ripening coupled with facet-selective capping. This structural transition induces a prominent bathochromic shift in the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) from 410 nm to ∼600 nm, driven by 2D shape anisotropy and in-plane dipolar modes. Spectroscopic (FTIR) and thermal (TGA) characterizations confirm dual-polymer surface stabilization, where starch binds via hydroxyl hydrogen bonding (redshifted from 3380 cm-1 to 3290 cm-1) and PVP undergoes physical adsorption (1655 cm-1 C[double bond, length as m-dash]O stretch), imparting high aqueous dispersion stability (-50 mV zeta potential). This study provides quantitative mechanistic insights into the green, shape-controlled sy

papers.title: Supramolecular assembly and membrane anchoring alter variant-induced SARS-CoV-2 Spike conformational dynamics.
papers.abstract: Viral surface glycoproteins function within crowded, membrane-anchored supramolecular assemblies, yet their dynamics are often inferred from soluble, engineered ectodomains. For SARS-CoV-2 Spike (S), this distinction is especially important because variant mutations evolved in the context of intact virions, not engineered trimers. Here, we combined cyclic ion mobility mass spectrometry (CIM-MS) for hydrogen deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDXMS) with computational weighted ensemble molecular dynamic (WE-MD) simulations to compare the conformational effects of SARS-CoV-2 mutations in two S protein constructs: soluble recombinant 2P S and full-length S displayed in virus-like particles (VLPs). Our results reveal that membrane anchoring and virion-like assembly substantially dampen global dynamic changes produced by variant mutations. In VLP S, D614G induced decreased dynamics across interprotomer contacts, whereas Omicron BA.1 mutations systematically reversed this decrease in dynamics in the S1 domain while preserving decreased dynamics near the fusion machinery. These effects are more spatially constrained than those observed in recombinant 2P S. Comparison of the 2 constructs further reveals that 2P substitutions alter native interprotomer communication. Recombinant S shows a predominantly fast-exchanging population in the receptor binding domain (RBD) hinge region, consistent with disruption of hydrogen-bonding and salt bridge networks that couple RBD motion to the trimer core. Thus, recombinant S captures important structural features of S without recapitulating the native conformational ensemble presented on virions. Together, these results show that the supramolecular context of S reshapes the conformational dynamics of variant evolution with direct implications for epitope presentation, antibody recognition, and interpretation of recombinant S structural studies.

papers.title: Microscopic Origins of Metal-Dependent pH Effects in Hydrogen Evolution: Metal-Water Interactions Dictate Proton Transfer Pathways.
papers.abstract: The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a prototypical proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) reaction, yet the atomistic origin of its metal-dependent pH effect remains unclear. Here, combining constant-potential ab initio molecular dynamics with in situ infrared spectroscopy, we unravel the microscopic origins of metal-dependent pH effects in HER catalysis on Pt(111) and Au(111). We reveal that HER kinetics are governed by two competing spatial proton transfer topologies associated with the Volmer water-dissociation step: a low-barrier cross-layer proton transfer (CLPT) pathway and a high-barrier intra-layer proton transfer (ILPT) pathway. For Pt(111), strong metal-water interactions yield a pH-responsive water network. Under acidic conditions, a balanced intra- and cross-layer hydrogen-bond network promotes the CLPT in the Volmer step, thereby accelerating HER kinetics. By contrast, alkaline media induce a rigid H-down interfacial water layer that favors the sluggish ILPT pathway. Conversely, weak metal-water interactions on Au(111) maintain a pH-insensitive, predominantly parallel-flat water orientation that restricts the Volmer step to cooperate only with the high-barrier ILPT in both acidic and alkaline solutions. Our findings establish a fundamental causal link among metal-water interactions, interfacial hydrogen-bonding network, proton transfer pathways, and HER kinetics, providing atomistic insight into the design of pH-robust electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Design and Analysis of a Bending-Torsion Coupled Bio-Inspired Claw Attachment Mechanism for Variable-Diameter Curved Surfaces.
papers.abstract: Reliable aerial perching on variable-diameter curved surfaces requires both sufficient grasping preload and conformal interfacial contact, whereas conventional underactuated bird-claw-inspired mechanisms primarily accommodate in-plane geometric variations and therefore have limited adaptability to surfaces with spatially varying curvature. This study presents a bending-torsion coupled bird-claw-inspired attachment mechanism for variable-diameter curved surfaces. The key design combines direction-selective compliant joints with a bilateral force-balanced tendon transmission, allowing asymmetric contact reactions to passively reorient individual claw segments. This passive reorientation improves interfacial conformity during grasping and provides more favorable contact and sealing conditions for dry adhesion and vacuum suction. A grasping-stability model was employed to optimize the key structural parameters, followed by mechanical characterization of the compliant joints and attachment tests on smooth acrylic cylinders with diameters of 60-120 mm and cones with apex angles of 20°-60°. The equivalent bending stiffness of the compliant joint was tunable from 0.2 to 1.0 N·mm/°, while high torsional compliance was maintained within the small-angle working range. The maximum circumferential attachment moment reached 1.65 N·m on a 120 mm diameter cylinder and 0.60 N·m on a 60° apex-angle cone. A manually controlled flight experiment further demonstrated successful perching on a 20° conical surface. These results demonstrate that bending-torsion coupled compliance can broaden the geometric adaptation range of underactuated claw-based attachment mechanisms and provide a feasible structural approach for aerial perching on variable-diameter curved surfaces.

papers.title: Water-Assisted Li+ Transport and cis-TFSI- Effects in Water-in-LiTFSI Electrolytes.
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
papers.abstract: Water-in-salt electrolytes are promising candidates for electrochemical devices. In this work, structures and dynamics of water-in-LiTFSI electrolytes are explored through large-scale atomistic molecular dynamics simulation employing a full-charge Drude polarizable force field with anO(N) -scaling random batch sum-of-Gaussians method for long-ranged electrostatic interactions. Disruption of the hydrogen bonding of bulk water and formation of LiTFSI networks in 21 m solution are observed. Particularly, the roles of cis and trans conformers of TFSI- are uncovered, and isomerization is found to occur in nanoseconds, on a similar time scale of Li+ escaping from the major cis-TFSI- conformers. Most water molecules are dynamically bound to Li+ with comparably rapid rotational motion in tens of picoseconds. Vehicular transport coupled to fast water dynamics and collective joining with the structural motion of Li+ along pathways of TFSI- cluster/network prevailed by cis-TFSI- are attributed to the appreciable Li+ conductivity in water-in-LiTFSI electrolytes.

papers.title: Asymmetric Alkylation of α-Cyanoketimines with Alkyl Bromides Catalyzed by Bis-Cinchonium Salts.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: The SN2 reaction constitutes one of the most fundamental bond-forming transformations in organic chemistry, finding numerous synthetic applications across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. However, the development of new catalysts for asymmetric SN2 reactions with nucleophiles beyond enolate derivatives remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the development of a new class of bis-cinchonium catalysts for an unprecedented enantioselective SN2 alkylation of cyanoketimines with alkyl bromides. This reaction features a broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby providing a useful approach to enantioenriched α,α-dialkyl aminonitriles. Computational studies revealed that the bis-cinchonium catalyst, through a network of weak bonding interactions, activated both cyanoketimines and alkyl bromides and preorganized them along the trajectory toward the transition state of an SN2 reaction.

papers.title: Long-Term Residential Care: Overall Planning and Design Framework Based on a Universal Design Approach.
papers.journal: Studies in health technology and informatics
papers.abstract: This paper draws on recent research that culminated in Universal Design (UD) guidelines for long-term residential care (LTRC) settings for older people in Ireland. Considering the broad spectrum of needs, impairments, and health conditions; the diversity of residents, staff, and visitors in LTRC; and a commitment to participation and co-creation, this research was underpinned by a UD approach. The project involved a range of Irish and international organisations and partners with expertise and lived experience in LTRC, UD, and the healthcare-built environment. As the research progressed, and as a range of complex and interconnected issues arose, it became apparent that a flexible overall framework was required to support the research and structure the guidelines. This paper focuses on this framework describing how it is informed by and reinforces a UD approach to LTRC planning and design.

papers.title: Mate preferences and the compatibility puzzle.
papers.abstract: Researchers and laypeople commonly assume that romantic attraction depends, at least in part, on whether potential partners possess the traits that a person says they want. Yet recent studies suggest that such preference-matching effects (Preference × Trait statistical interactions) are often surprisingly small or even absent. Possible psychological explanations include (i) mate choice is multivariate, and so the matching effect for any given trait is heavily constrained, and (ii) traits permit flexible interpretations, in that the same trait can be interpreted differently depending on the partner to whom the trait belongs. Compatibility may derive not mainly from the matching of preferences and traits but rather from the way that two people recurrently extend and build upon shared positive experiences over time.

papers.title: Trajectories of romantic partners' social functioning across the military deployment cycle.
papers.journal: Journal of family psychology : JFP : journal of the Division of Family Psychology of the American Psychological Association (Division 43)
papers.abstract: Research has documented adverse psychiatric effects of wartime deployment on military spouses/partners, yet studies examining partners' quality of life beyond symptomatology are lacking. This study identified trajectories of social functioning among partners of military personnel across an 18-month deployment cycle. National Guard soldiers and their spouses/partners (N = 1,028 dyads) completed assessments 2-5 months predeployment to Kuwait/Iraq or Afghanistan (Time 1), at 4 months (Time 2) and 8 months (Time 3) during deployment, and 2-3 months postdeployment (Time 4). Latent class growth modeling revealed four distinct trajectories among partners: (a) stable high (72.1%), characterized by consistently high social functioning throughout; (b) recovery (13.3%), experiencing deployment-related decline in social functioning followed by postdeployment improvement; (c) stable moderate (12.9%), demonstrating consistently moderate functioning; and (d) declining (1.7%), showing marked decreases in functioning across the cycle. Trajectories were then compared on partner and soldier predeployment characteristics. Compared to the stable high group, stable moderate partners-and their soldiers-reported higher negative emotionality/neuroticism and lower deployment readiness, relationship satisfaction, and social support. Recovery partners differed only in their own higher neuroticism. In contrast, declining partners differed primarily on external factors, reporting more potentially traumatic events, less social support, and being partnered to soldiers with higher neuroticism. Thus, partners of National Guard soldiers follow diverse social adjustment pathways, challenging monolithic assumptions about military family resilience. These findings advance the field's understanding of the variable ways that partners respond to deployment and may be used to optimize delivery of programs targeting different dimensions of military family well-being. papers.title: Metabolic State Machines and Nutritional Ecology: A New Framework for Osteosarcoma Therapy.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor of children and adolescents, yet survival has plateaued for four decades despite surgery and multi-agent chemotherapy. This review argues that the clinically decisive feature of osteosarcoma metabolism is not a fixed commitment to glycolysis or to oxidative phosphorylation, but the capacity to move between metabolic states under hypoxia, acidosis, nutrient fluctuation, and treatment stress. We develop two connected frameworks. The first is a metabolic state machine, in which metabolic phenotypes are treated as stress-responsive states that are coupled to chemoresistance, radioresistance, metastatic adaptation, immune escape, and ferroptosis vulnerability. The second is a nutritional ecology of the bone microenvironment, which explains how stromal and immune cells exchange and compete for lactate, amino acids, and other substrates, and why blocking a single metabolic node is usually compensated. We then map the principal actionable modules, including lactate transport, nucleotide and serine metabolism, redox homeostasis, ferroptosis, and therapy-induced immunometabolic escape, onto candidate stratifiers and pharmacodynamic readouts. The framework is intended less as a catalogue of enzymes than as a practical route to state-matched, dynamically monitored combination therapy.

papers.title: Regional Histological Anatomy of the Supraperiosteal Tissues of the Oral Cavity: Implications for Periodontal Flap Surgery and Periosteal Releasing Incisions.
papers.abstract: Periodontal and implant procedures increasingly involve tissue planes superficial to the periosteum, yet their regional anatomy remains poorly understood. This study conducted a histological investigation of the supraperiosteal anatomy of the oral cavity and its implications for periosteal releasing incisions (PRIs). Intraoral dissection of the mimetic muscle was performed using a fresh anatomical donor. Subsequently, maxillary and mandibular incisor, premolar, and molar regions from five formalin-fixed donors were examined histologically using Masson's trichrome staining. Muscular, neural, vascular, and connective tissue structures within 5 mm of the facial alveolar bone surface were evaluated. Supraperiosteal tissue architecture differed markedly by region. Muscular, neural, and vascular structures showed distinct region-specific distributions. The mental nerve and its branches were identified in the mandibular premolar region, whereas facial and buccal vessels were present near the bone surface in the posterior regions. Muscle attachment and intervening connective tissue also varied regionally. Structures potentially injured during PRI and their associated risks are region-dependent. PRI should therefore be guided by region-specific anatomy and the tissues requiring release for sufficient flap mobility rather than by a predetermined incision depth alone.

papers.title: Opening the window for immunotherapy in pancreatic cancer.
papers.abstract: KRAS inhibitors (KRASi) are reshaping the treatment of aggressive tumors such as pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), but it is appreciated that patients will eventually acquire resistance through multiple pathways. To avoid this outcome, there is much effort to identify combination therapies that take advantage of the 'window-of-opportunity' permitted from KRAS inhibition. Tumor cell-intrinsic targeting - as a result of KRASi - results in altered immune and stromal features within the PDAC tumor site that could allow for improved, non-KRAS-targeted, treatment efficacy. Qiang and colleagues investigate the potential of pairing KRASi with immunotherapy - here, an IL-21 mimic - for therapeutic benefit during this 'open window' phase of the KRASi-induced tumor debulking. IL-21 promotes a CD4 T cell response that requires both conventional type 2 dendritic cells (cDC2s) and interferon (IFN)-γ, but not direct tumor cell recognition via major histocompatibility complex (MHC). This work fits in a series of studies highlighting the ability to drive PDAC tumor rejection through cytokines derived from CD4, but not CD8, T cells. These findings highlight a divergence from more 'traditional' immunotherapeutic responses, where cytotoxic CD8 T cells have historically dominated tumor control. Identifying alternative paths towards targeting PDAC may be beneficial - and points towards cell types and modalities that could be leveraged for clinical benefit as the field identifies potential combinatorial partners for KRASi and more patients start receiving these drugs.

papers.title: The Silent Half of the Couple: Partner Sexual and Psychosocial Outcomes in Penile Cancer.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND/AIM: Surgical treatment of penile cancer, ranging from organ-sparing techniques to partial or total penectomy, profoundly affects sexual function, body image and psychosocial wellbeing. Although patient-reported outcomes have been extensively studied, the experience of the sexual partner remains largely unexplored. This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize the available evidence on sexual, psychosocial and relational outcomes reported directly by partners of men treated surgically for penile cancer, across the full spectrum of oncological penile surgery. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed/MEDLINE indexed literature was searched, supplemented by citation chasing of reference lists of relevant reviews and targeted grey-literature screening, with no date restriction. Studies were eligible if they reported outcome data collected directly from partners of men who underwent any oncological surgical procedure for penile cancer. RESULTS: Of 25 records screened, three studies met the formal eligibility criteria for outcome data collected directly from partners; a fourth study, in which partner-related themes emerged only from patient interviews without direct partner sampling, was retained solely as supporting contextual evidence and was not counted among the formally included studies or in the PRISMA-ScR flow. Partner sexual dysfunction was reported in up to 5 of 10 evaluable partners (50%), and continued couple sexual activity after surgery ranged from 17 of 29 partners (58.6%) at 12 months in one cohort to 12 of 14 partners (85.7%) in another. Instruments used to assess partner outcomes were markedly heterogeneous, and no dyadic-specific validated instrument for penile cancer exists. CONCLUSION: Evidence on partner outcomes after penile cancer surgery is scarce, heterogeneous and almost entirely observational, despite broad agre

papers.title: Association between violence against women and intimate partner characteristics: a population-based study conducted in Vitória, Espírito Santo.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: to analyze the association between violence against women and the sociodemographic and behavioral characteristics of their intimate partners. METHOD: cross-sectional study conducted with 1,086 women aged 18 years or older who had an intimate partner in the past 24 months. The World Health Organization instrument on violence against women, validated for use in Brazil, was used to classify psychological, physical and sexual violence. The intimate partners' sociodemographic and behavioral characteristics were collected. The results were presented as Prevalence Ratios and their respective 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: women whose partners were ≥41 years old had a 19% lower prevalence of psychological and physical violence. Higher prevalence of such abuse was found among women whose partners were black and who consumed alcohol. Psychological violence was 25%, 17%, and 30% higher, respectively, among those whose partners did not have a paid job, smoked or were former smokers. Physical violence was 73% more frequent among participants whose partners belonged to the first tertile of the per capita family income. Psychological, physical or sexual victimization was higher among those who felt fear of their partners (PR: 1.42; 95% CI: 1.24-1.64; PR: 2.52; 95% CI: 2.02-3.13; PR: 1.97; 95% CI: 1.48-2.63) and with controlling partners (PR: 1.48; 95% CI: 1.29-1.70; PR: 1.30; 95% CI: 1.04-1.62; PR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.09-1.86). CONCLUSION: sociodemographic and behavioral characteristics of partners increase women's vulnerability to violence.

papers.title: [Factors associated with transitions in the status of intimate partner violence in older adults: the EpiFloripa Idoso longitudinal study].
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the association between previous exposure to violence, depressive symptoms, and alcohol use and changes in intimate partner violence status in older adults in EpiFloripa Idoso. This longitudinal study analyzed cohort data by multinomial logistic regression. It categorized intimate partner violence according to violence (perpetration and victimization) status change over time. Its final sample consisted of 336 participants (those who answered the instrument in both time measurements). The following factors were associated with the onset of the perpetration: depressive symptoms with a history of violence (OR = 4.93; 95%CI: 1.10-21.30) and high alcohol consumption (OR = 2.77; 95%CI: 1.12-6.84). Perpetration continuity was associated with depressive symptoms with (OR = 8.09; 95%CI: 2.34-27.97) and without (OR = 4.44; 95%CI: 1.18-16.60) history of violence. The onset of victimization was associated with depressive symptoms with a history of violence (OR = 9.40; 95%CI: 1.94-45.47). Victimization continuity was associated with depressive symptoms with (OR = 10.20; 95%CI: 2.48-41.94) and without history of violence (OR = 8.04; 95%CI: 1.91-33.81). This study finds the need for integrated actions in mental health and in coping with violence in children and older adults as they can help to prevent future intimate partner violence. Limitations include self-reported measures, potential recall bias, limitations of the instrument for older adults, and analytical restrictions due to the sample size. papers.title: All About Trust: Attitudes Toward Mandatory Reporting Among Victims and Perpetrators of Intimate Partner Violence.
papers.abstract: The study aimed to examine attitudes toward mandatory reporting of intimate partner violence (MR-IPV) among 86 victims and 41 perpetrators of intimate partner violence (IPV) in Norway. Descriptive results were examined, and multivariate ordinal regression was used to examine differences between victims and perpetrators, and predictors of attitudes. Overall, victims and perpetrators were positive toward MR-IPV, and there was high consensus on slightly more than half the statements. Arguments that MR-IPV is unwanted and can decrease trust and help-seeking were not supported in the study, but concerns that MR-IPV can lead to worse IPV highlight the complexity of MR-IPV and the importance of considering safety issues when help services intervene. Victims and perpetrators only reported different attitudes regarding two aspects of MR-IPV. More victims agreed that MR-IPV can lead to worse IPV and more disagreed that MR-IPV is a safeguard for perpetrators. The most consistent predictor of attitudes was trust in health services, with more positive attitudes among those reporting higher trust. The results support MR-IPV as an important intervention for preventing IPV. The association between attitudes and trust could indicate a need for viewing MR-IPV in its broader context, taking into account the general help service response.

papers.title: Indirect Effects of a Prenatal Intimate Partner Violence Intervention on Infant Socioemotional Functioning: Examining the Pregnant Moms' Empowerment Program.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical child and adolescent psychology : the official journal for the Society of Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology, American Psychological Association, Division 53
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The current study evaluated whether previously established intervention-related improvements in maternal psychological functioning (i.e. IPV revictimization, depression) and caregiving (i.e. empathy, developmentally appropriate parenting expectations, observed parenting sensitivity) indirectly impact infant temperament (i.e. Surgency/Extraversion, Negative Affectivity, Orienting/Regulation) and observed affect. METHOD: Data were drawn from a quasi-randomized trial with N = 137 pregnant women who had experienced IPV. RESULTS: Results indicated that there were some indirect benefits of the PMEP for infants. Specifically, intervention-related decreases in maternal IPV revictimization contributed to more positive observed infant affect, while intervention-related decreases in maternal depressive symptoms led to lower levels of infant Negative Affectivity. CONCLUSIONS: Study findings highlight the emergence of promising evidence to support the intergenerational benefits of PMEP for infants born to IPV-exposed mothers, suggesting that early intervention for families is not only possible but also likely engenders benefits across the family system.

papers.title: Misogyny and Criminal Thinking in a Sample of Men Convicted of IPV.
papers.abstract: This study empirically examined the relationship between criminal thinking and misogyny in a sample of 503 heterosexual men convicted of intimate partner violence (IPV) and referred to a community-based batterer intervention program. Drawing on survey data collected over two years, the study sought to identify the emotional and cognitive components of misogyny and assess their connection to criminal thinking. Findings demonstrated a significant association between criminal thinking and misogynistic attitudes, providing preliminary support for integrating theories of misogyny with theories of criminal thinking. These findings contribute to theory development and suggest that interventions targeting both constructs may enhance rehabilitation outcomes following IPV convictions.

papers.title: Gender-based violence in obstetric and gynecologic care: Secondary victimization, ethics, and trauma-informed practice-scoping review.
papers.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
papers.abstract: Domestic, sexual, and gender-based violence (DSGBV) affects between 27% and 35% of women worldwide. The rate of this type of violence is higher in many low- and middle-income nations, and it exceeds 37% for women living in those countries. Many DSGBV survivors begin their healthcare experience at an obstetrics or gynecology (OB-GYN) office. Survivors might experience several barriers to receiving appropriate OB-GYN treatment because of failures to screen, secondary victimization, provider behavior, ethical dilemmas, and structural barriers; these barriers can affect the survivor's ability to disclose to a care provider, receive continuous care, and achieve long-term health outcomes. A search of the scientific literature was performed using PubMed and Scopus databases, gathering peer-reviewed articles that focused on DSGBV epidemiology, reproductive health outcomes of victims, secondary victimization in healthcare environments, trauma-informed care, ethical principles, and factors related to institutions that provide OB-GYN services to women. This review followed a scoping review methodology. The authors used a dual-reviewer systematic search, screening, and data-extraction process, which has been described in the methods section. Collected data were thematically synthesized to understand the power imbalance between OB-GYN practitioners and their patients, the professional behaviors of OB-GYN providers, the privacy dilemmas that exist between OB-GYN providers and their patients, how the training models for OB-GYN practitioners in high-income settings are applied to low-income and middle-income settings, and the adaptation strategies that can be implemented to provide trauma-informed care in low-income and middle-income settings. Domestic, sexual, and gender-based violence (DSGBV) exposure is related to an increase of 1.5 to 2.0 times in unintended pregnancy, 1.7 times in unsafe abortion, and approximately 2.0 times in high-prevalence areas HIV risk. papers.title: Using Safe and Ethical Technology to Prevent and Respond to Sexual Violence and Intimate Partner Violence During Adolescence and Young Adulthood: Identifying Evidence, Best Practices, and Pathways Forward-An International, English-Language Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Adolescents and young adults face high risks of sexual violence and intimate partner violence (SV/IPV). While technology can help mitigate SV/IPV, it also has the potential to enable abuse. Ensuring the safe and ethical use of technology in SV/IPV prevention is crucial. To synthesize evidence on the use of technology for the prevention and response to SV/IPV among adolescents and young adults, with a focus on assessing safety and ethical considerations. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language studies published globally between 2008 and 2025 and describing the use of technology to prevent or respond to SV/IPV among youth aged 10 to 24 years of all genders. Covidence was used to screen studies, with two authors applying the eligibility criteria. The included literature was synthesized on a prepared data extraction form and thematically analyzed as a narrative to identify emergent findings. Fourteen reviewed references highlighted two main uses of technology: (a) preventing SV/IPV through awareness, safety plans, and emergency alerts, and (b) responding to SV/IPV by connecting users to support services. Common safety considerations included informed consent and user anonymity, but concerns were raised about data privacy, inability to use technology discreetly around perpetrators, and non-inclusive content limiting access for vulnerable populations. Although some technologies describe safety and ethical considerations, there are gaps in structured protocols and frameworks to guide ethical development and the inclusion of specific features that safeguard adolescents and young adults against unintended harm.

papers.title: Social determinants of partner and non-partner sexual violence against women in Chile: a population-based multilevel analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sexual violence against women is a major public health problem in Latin America, yet evidence on its social determinants is scarce and often conflates partner and non-partner forms. We characterised determinants of intimate partner sexual violence (IPSV), non-partner sexual assault (NPSA), and non-partner sexual harassment (NPSH) in Chile and compared their risk profiles. METHODS: We analysed pooled 2017 and 2020 rounds of the Chilean National Survey on Violence in the Family and Other Settings, representative of urban women aged 15 years or older; fieldwork preceded Chile's first COVID-19 case. We fitted multilevel logistic regression for past-year outcomes, women nested in municipalities. FINDINGS: The sample comprised 13,128 women (8335 for IPSV models). Past-year prevalence was 2.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.4-3.3) for IPSV, 2.5% (2.1-3.0) for NPSA, and 11.3% (10.4-12.3) for NPSH. IPSV was associated with relational factors: dominant relationship (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 6.40, 4.68-8.76) and partner violence elsewhere (2.79, 1.75-4.43); between-municipality variance was negligible. NPSA and NPSH concentrated in younger women and the Metropolitan Region (OR 2.92 [2.00-4.28] and 2.29 [1.77-2.96]); both were associated with social participation (1.49 [1.11-2.00] and 1.26 [1.09-1.46]). Childhood sexual abuse was associated with all three (OR 2.05 [1.45-2.89], 3.03 [2.20-4.20], and 2.06 [1.72-2.46]). Reported non-partner victimisation rose between 2017 and 2020, pre-pandemic. INTERPRETATION: Risk profiles differed: relational and life-course for IPSV, age-graded and metropolitan for NPSA and NPSH; childhood sexual abuse was common to all three, supporting trauma-informed responses. papers.title: Investigating the Relationship Between Self-Compassion and Marital Satisfaction in Pregnant Women With Depression: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Antenatal depression is a prevalent mental health concern that can adversely affect marital relationships. Self-compassion has emerged as a potential protective factor in improving psychological health and interpersonal relationships. This cross-sectional study aimed to investigate the relationship between self-compassion and marital satisfaction in pregnant women with depression. METHODS: In this cross-sectional analytical study, 240 pregnant women with depression were selected through convenience sampling from healthcare centers in Kermanshah, Iran. Depression was assessed using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) with a cutoff score > 12, and all participants met DSM-5 criteria for depressive symptoms. Participants completed the Self-Compassion Scale-Long Form, Hudson's Marital Satisfaction Inventory, and a demographic questionnaire. The cross-sectional design and convenience sampling limit the generalizability of findings. RESULTS: The mean age was 27.68 years (SD = 4.63). Logistic regression revealed that a one-unit increase in total self-compassion score was associated with a 10% increase in the odds of being in the satisfied group (OR = 1.10; 95% CI: 1.07-1.12; p < 0.001). "Common human experience" showed the strongest association (OR = 1.64; 95% CI: 1.43-1.87; p < 0.001). Positive components-self-kindness (r = 0.552), common humanity (r = 0.561), and well-being (r = 0.519)-had significant positive correlations with marital satisfaction, while negative components-self-judgment (r = -0.462), isolation (r = -0.506), and over-identification (r = -0.446)-showed significant negative correlations (all p < 0.001). papers.title: Paths to better emotion regulation in couple therapy: Exploring ACEs and attachment.
papers.journal: Psychotherapy research : journal of the Society for Psychotherapy Research
papers.abstract: Objective: Emotion regulation (ER) is increasingly recognized as a key mechanism in couple therapy. However, little is known about how ER changes across treatment or how early adverse events and current attachment experiences shape this process. Methods: Using a sample of 308 married individuals in couple therapy, this study examined changes in ER difficulties across a total of 24 sessions. We also tested whether adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and current attachment insecurity (anxiety, avoidance) predicted baseline levels and changes in ER. Results: Multilevel modelling showed a small but significant decline in ER difficulties across sessions. Both ACEs and insecure attachment were associated with higher baseline ER difficulties. However, only avoidant attachment predicted greater improvement over time. ACEs and attachment anxiety were unrelated to change. Variance analysis revealed that most variation in ER occurred between individuals (70%) and within individuals over time (23%), with minimal variance at the couple (5%) and therapist (2%) levels. Conclusion: Findings support ER as a dynamic treatment target and underscore the importance of assessing developmental history and current attachment insecurity to guide intervention.
